name: Blood Smear
desc: A peripheral blood film under the objective, stained Wright-Giemsa: the field packed with erythrocytes as salmon biconcave discs each carrying the pale central pallor that gives red cells their donut look, while the stage pans slowly and endlessly so the smear drifts and cells wrap across the frame. Scattered through them are leukocytes -- neutrophils with a dark multilobed nucleus, lymphocytes with one round nucleus, the odd eosinophil dusted orange -- larger cells crossing the field, plus tiny platelet flecks; the pan runs on incommensurate rates so it never re-phases and slow focus makes the discs breathe. Offered as classic Giemsa stain, glowing dark-field rings, a grey scanning-EM relief, or a false-colour oxygenation map.

scale.doc: magnification - fewer, larger cells, guaranteed visible change
